note: Lean starts from an arbitrary ψ mod q and passes to its primitive χ; the identity is used at n=1 only, with $c_r(1)=\mu(r)$ built into `gauss_induced`, and no Ramanujan sum $c_r(n)$ is named.

snippet.text:
set χ := ψ.primitiveCharacter
  have hψ : DirichletCharacter.changeLevel hcq χ = ψ := DirichletCharacter.changeLevel_primitiveCharacter ψ
  set r := q / c with hr
  have hqr : q = c * r := (Nat.mul_div_cancel' hcq).symm
  have hr1 : 1 ≤ r := Nat.pos_of_ne_zero (by
    intro h0; rw [h0, mul_zero] at hqr; exact NeZero.ne q hqr)
  set f : ℕ → ℂ := fun b => χ (b : ZMod c)
  have hτ : gaussSum ψ ZMod.stdAddChar = (μ r : ℂ) * f r * gaussSum χ ZMod.stdAddChar := by
    rw [gaussSum_eq_sum_range, gaussSum_eq_sum_range]
    have h1 : ∑ b ∈ range q, ψ (b : ZMod q) * e (b / q) =
        ∑ b ∈ (range (c * r)).filter (fun b => Nat.Coprime b (c * r)), f b * e (b / (c * r)) := by
      have hqR : (c : ℝ) * r = q := by rw [hqr]; push_cast; ring
      rw [sum_filter, ← hqr, hqR]
      refine sum_congr rfl fun b _ => ?_
      rw [← hψ, changeLevel_apply_natCast]
      split_ifs <;> simp [f]
    rw [h1, gauss_induced (Nat.pos_of_ne_zero hc0) hr1 f]

proof_context.conclusion: Sets `χ := ψ.primitiveCharacter` (modulus the conductor `c`, `r = q/c`) and writes `τ(ψ) = μ(r) χ(r) τ(χ)` via `gauss_induced`.

snippet.text:
/-- **Gauss sum of an induced character**: for `f` periodic mod `N`, completely multiplicative,
and zero off the residues coprime to `N`,
`Σ_{b < Nr, (b, Nr) = 1} f(b) e(b/Nr) = μ(r) f(r) Σ_{c < N} f(c) e(c/N)`. -/
theorem gauss_induced {N r : ℕ} (hN : 1 ≤ N) (hr : 1 ≤ r) (f : ℕ → ℂ)
    (hper : ∀ b, f (b + N) = f b) (hmul : ∀ a b, f (a * b) = f a * f b)
    (hzero : ∀ b, ¬ Nat.Coprime b N → f b = 0) :
    ∑ b ∈ (range (N * r)).filter (fun b => Nat.Coprime b (N * r)), f b * e (b / (N * r)) =
      μ r * f r * ∑ c ∈ range N, f c * e (c / N) := by

proof_context.conclusion: `Σ_{b<Nr,(b,Nr)=1} f(b)e(b/Nr) = μ(r) f(r) Σ_{c<N} f(c)e(c/N)` for multiplicative `f` mod `N` (no primitivity needed).
